title: A more professional hand
question: Safer re-roll: three professional directions plus the category standard. Pick one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Spec Sheet
options.lineage: engineering datasheets: the front page of a component spec
options.thesis: You, documented like a well-made component: features, specifications, applications, revision history.
options.viewport: A header band with your name as the part title, then Features beside a figure of your flagship system; real tables below.
options.risk: Reads dry if the tables are set without care; it relies on typography doing the work.

options.label: Release Notes
options.lineage: versioned product changelogs and release notes
options.thesis: Your career read as release notes: every role and project an entry of what shipped.
options.viewport: Your name and one line, then a dated rail down the left with each project and role as a release entry.
options.risk: Very close to how developer-tool sites already look; familiar by design.

options.label: Unigrid
options.lineage: Vignelli's Unigrid for park brochures: black title band, strict modular grid
options.thesis: A disciplined modular grid under one black title band, where the work does all the talking.
options.viewport: A black band carrying your name across the top; below, a strict grid of project panels with real screenshots.
options.risk: Austere; without strong screenshots it can look empty.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The developer-portfolio canon at full craft, measured against Brittany Chiang, Lee Robinson and Paco Coursey.
canonCard.viewport: A sticky left column with name, role and section links; experience and projects scroll on the right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from countless developer portfolios by design.
